title: Slightly Frowning Face Emoji 🙁 Meaning: A Little Sad
description: The slightly frowning face emoji 🙁 is the mildest sad face, a small frown for small letdowns. Learn what it means, how to respond, and how it differs from ☹️.
summary: The 🙁 slightly frowning face means mild sadness or disappointment. It is the emoji form of typing :( and suits everyday letdowns: canceled plans, bad weather, a friend leaving early. It shows the sender is unhappy without drama, and it often expresses sympathy for someone else's small misfortune.
meaning: Two dots and a shallow downward curve are all there is to this face, and its meaning is equally modest. 🙁 says that's a shame. It fits the ordinary disappointments of a day: the cafe is out of your usual order, the package is delayed, a friend cannot make it. Nothing is seriously wrong, but the sender wishes things were otherwise.

It is the nearest emoji to the typed frown :( that people used for decades before picture characters, and it keeps that plain, unshowy feel. There are no tears, no furrowed brows and no sweat. For many users that restraint is the appeal. It registers a feeling honestly and then lets the conversation carry on.

A second common use is sympathy. When someone tells you about a rough morning or a minor setback, replying 🙁 means I am sorry that happened. It mirrors their mood at a low intensity. For heavier news it can seem too slight, and people usually move up to a crying face or a heart.

Because it is so understated, it sometimes carries more than it shows. A person who is quite hurt but unwilling to say so may send only 🙁, particularly to a partner. It can also come across as a little passive, a way of signaling displeasure and waiting for the other person to ask. The relationship and timing tell you which.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It ends messages about small bad news, like I have to work Saturday 🙁, and answers them too. It is quick and unambiguous. Sent alone in reply to a cancellation, it means they are disappointed and would appreciate a new plan or at least an acknowledgment.

contexts.label: From a partner or crush
contexts.body: It tends to mean they miss you, wanted more time or were hoping for a different answer. I thought you'd call 🙁 is a soft complaint. It is rarely angry. Responding warmly, instead of defensively, is usually what they are looking for.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: It is acceptable for minor regrets, such as a colleague being out sick or a meeting clash, and it shows you care. Avoid it when giving feedback or declining a request, where it may look like you are using sadness to pressure someone.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: People comment it on posts about a favorite show ending, a restaurant closing or an injury to a player. It expresses a shared, low-level sadness. It is less performative than the loudly crying face, so it often reads as more sincere.

examples.text: It's supposed to rain all weekend 🙁

examples.meaning: Sad that someone will be missing.
Feeling a bit lonely and wanting the other person there.
Sad that something enjoyable is ending.

combos.meaning: Sad and hurt; more feeling than the frown alone admits.
Gloomy weather and a mood to match.
Sorry to hear that; offering comfort.
Shyly sad, often when asking for attention or forgiveness.

confusedWith.difference: ☹️ has a deeper, wider frown and reads as noticeably sadder. It is also an older symbol that can display in plain black and white. 🙁 is the lighter option and always appears as a color emoji.
😕 tips its frown to one side, adding puzzlement or uncertainty. 🙁 is symmetrical and simply a bit sad. When you know what you feel, use 🙁.
😞 looks down with closed eyes and conveys real dejection or regret. 🙁 keeps its eyes open and its feelings small. One is deflated; the other is merely bummed.

avoid: Do not use it for serious losses or bereavement, where it seems inadequate.
Avoid sending it repeatedly to guilt someone into changing their mind.
Skip it in formal complaints; describe the problem instead.
design: A yellow face with two plain oval eyes and a small, shallow frown. It has no eyebrows or other features. Every major platform draws it in nearly the same way. It is deliberately the counterpart of the slightly smiling face, with the same eyes and the mouth curved the other way.

faqs.q: What does 🙁 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: That they are a bit sad or disappointed, often about not seeing you or about something you said. It is gentle, not angry. A kind reply or a suggestion to make up for it is usually well received.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🙁 and ☹️?
faqs.a: Degree. 🙁 is a slight frown for minor disappointment. ☹️ is a full frown for stronger unhappiness. They also differ technically: ☹️ is a much older text symbol, while 🙁 was created as an emoji.

It can be if it is used to signal displeasure while refusing to explain. Most of the time it is a sincere, low-key expression of sadness. If someone sends it without context, asking what is wrong clears it up.

In spirit, yes. It is the closest emoji match for the typed frown, with the same simple eyes and downturned mouth. Some apps automatically replace :( with a frowning emoji, though which one appears depends on the app.
